dimensions.label: John McCain's public pro-life stance
dimensions.description: John McCain was a U.S. Senator and presidential candidate who publicly identified as pro-life, meaning he opposed abortion. This stance was a significant part of his political identity and was used in political campaigns and public discourse. The meme references this specific political position to create a contrast with his death.

dimensions.label: John McCain's death
dimensions.description: John McCain died on August 25, 2018, at the age of 81. His death was widely reported in the media and was a significant national event. The meme uses his death as a punchline to imply hypocrisy in his pro-life claims, which is a form of posthumous criticism.

dimensions.label: Pro-life political position
dimensions.description: The pro-life position is a political and moral stance that opposes abortion, often grounded in the belief that life begins at conception. It is a major issue in U.S. politics, particularly in the context of the Republican Party and conservative movements. The meme relies on the public understanding of this political position to make its point.

dimensions.label: Meme trope: juxtaposing claims with contradiction
dimensions.description: This meme uses a common internet trope of juxtaposing a person's public claim or identity with a contrasting event (in this case, death) to imply hypocrisy or insincerity. The meme format relies on the viewer's understanding of this rhetorical device to deliver its message.

dimensions.label: Posthumous political criticism
dimensions.description: The meme leverages the death of a public figure to criticize their political beliefs or actions. This is a form of posthumous criticism that can be seen as disrespectful or emotionally manipulative, as it uses the deceased person's mortality as a punchline. This trope is common in political memes and satire.
